grid_spec.note: Cartesian lr×emb×dropout = 24 configs; identical for every trainable model (GRUProbe, AttnProbe) per dataset. RAGR-lite is not part of this equal-budget trainable grid. GRUProbe has no dropout module (dropout grid is a no-op for GRU). max_epochs=10, patience=2 (see docs/DEVIATIONS.md).
grid_spec.extension_from_prior_freeze: Added emb=256 and lr=0.002 once after emb=128 edge winners

primary.clustering: preregistered; train/text-only (never eval sequences); two methods with agreement rule

excluded_notes.ragr_lite: N/A on ASSIST/XES; not full DAG RAGR

minimum_models_for_reversal_claim.rule: A cross-slice rank reversal is claimable only when the full required set is evaluated on the same learner-disjoint split and fixed sample indices; attn is not required.

budget_statement.note: Markov is not given the 24-config grid; it fits transition counts on train only.

attn_probe_architecture.library_validation: none — not checked against SASRec / RecBole / authors' code
attn_probe_architecture.exclusion_reason: Unvalidated local probe; do not treat as SASRec. Documented for exploratory comparison only.
attn_probe_architecture.positional_encoding: learned nn.Embedding(max_len, emb); added to token embeddings
attn_probe_architecture.causal_mask: triu boolean mask (diagonal=1) passed to TransformerEncoder
attn_probe_architecture.prediction_head: Linear(emb, n_items) on last position; embeddings not tied

assistments.sensitivity_note: Primary clustering uses skill_name MiniLM; no train-only fallback needed. Composite tokens = mean of member skill embeddings.

xes3g5m.fallback_reason: XES3G5M question_level CSVs expose question ids/KC tags only — no question stem text for MiniLM

prior_peeking_disclosure: Follow-up 3 inspected these datasets before preregistration; freeze uses a new seed/split

skill_construction.rule: groupby order_id; skills = sorted unique skill_id (>=0); composite item id = '_'.join(skills); primary = first of sorted skills
skill_construction.why_n_items_150_vs_123_atomic: Freeze ranking unit uses COMPOSITE skill tokens (150 distinct after collapse), not the 123 atomic skill_ids. Composites arise from multi-skill order_ids.

markov_order1.budget_note: First-order item→item successor counts on train only; no embedding/LR grid. Listed as parameter-light in the H-rev budget statement (not equal-grid).

grid_spec.note: Cartesian lr×emb×dropout = 24 configs; identical for every trainable model per dataset. max_epochs=10, patience=2 (see docs/DEVIATIONS.md).
grid_spec.extension_from_prior_freeze: Added emb=256 and lr=0.002 once after emb=128 edge winners

equal_tuning_budget.validation_metric_for_selection: val non-repeat R@5; among configs within 0.005 of best, lowest val CE

display_names.attn_probe: attention-based next-item probe (exploratory; excluded from H-rev)

question_order_structure.interpretation: Non-trivial fraction of steps advance to the next question in the dataset's sorted question-id order (~same as raw id+1). Combined with very low continue rate, sequence probes can hit high non-repeat R@5 by learning quiz/curriculum order rather than spaced revisit structure.

xes3g5m.curriculum_order_note: Question-level H-rev is curriculum-order-structured: empirical mode successor share≈0.350; global-order successor≈0.196. Native-unit contrasts are descriptive; primary confirmatory unit is cluster-matched.

assistments.note: k=120 is usable but near-native: only 150 composite tokens (used clusters at k=120 were 106).

junyi_timed.note: k=800 of n_items=835 is feasible but close to the native catalog

clustering_contrast_rule.rule: A clustering-method contrast (text vs train-only co-occurrence) counts only if both methods are defined on that dataset and they agree on the confirmatory claim (same sign / same ranking conclusion). XES has no text method → method-agreement contrasts are N/A.

preprereg_fixes.h_rev_losing_to_markov: If GRU loses to Markov at a unit, that unit cannot claim a learned H-rev win; a 1-step table already captures the regularity. Native XES is descriptive.

gru_markov_paired_ci.slice: validation sequences; same max_seqs cap as freeze

h_rev_implication.what_losing_to_markov_means: H-rev asks whether a probe's ranking vs baselines reverses when the action unit changes (native vs matched clusters). Markov order-1 is the parameter-light 1-step successor table. If GRU loses to Markov at a unit, that unit's GRU 'win' vs popularity/recency is not a learned-structure win: a count table already captures the regularity (sticky or curriculum-order). A confirmatory H-rev claim at that unit cannot treat GRU as beating the required baseline set. Native XES (7,439 questions, mode successor ≈0.35, GRU 0.614 vs Markov 0.739 at freeze) is therefore descriptive. The informative contrast is the cluster unit, where GRU can still beat Markov.
